message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `layout: sequence` (sequence diagrams) — byte-identical to the original. Participants (any node: boxes, icons as actors, cyl, slant…) across the top, lifelines, messages top-to-bottom in source order (`->` calls open activation bars, `-->` returns, `~>` async, self-messages `pay -> pay`, labels), `activation: none`, frames `|loop|`, `|alt|` with `|else|` branches, `|opt|`, notes `|note| { place: over a b | left of … }`, participant paint flowing onto lifelines and bars, gaps (`.lini-sequence` gap 32 32), errors such as `'|alt|' belongs in a 'layout: sequence'`, auto-created participants, layout/scene as root (`{ layout: sequence }`) and possibly nested `|sequence|` blocks. `executable desugar FILE` shows how these lower; the repo's desugar implementation (src/desugar/*) already reproduces sequence lowering text — reuse its understanding. Messages are links in `ctx.links` (see ARCH.md); the general link renderer/router (src/links.rs, src/route.rs) is for ordinary diagrams — in a sequence the messages are drawn by your module instead (reuse marker/label/mask helpers from links.rs where they match; the label-cut mask id hashing is solved there, see links.rs). Put your code in new module(s) (e.g. src/sequence.rs) with minimal hooks in layout.rs/render.rs/links.rs.

Test files: /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples prop_activation, prop_place, skill_04, spec_31, spec_32 (error), spec_55, blocks/skill_004, blocks/spec_031, blocks/spec_055; test_samples/sequence.lini. Write many synthetic snippets in /tmp/<you>/ to pin down spacing, bar nesting, self-message loops, frame geometry/labels, note placement, label positions/masks, multi-line labels, colours. Note: some sequence paths print raw f64 values (e.g. `-9.29249999999999`) rather than 4-decimal format — reproduce that exactly.

Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-seq/executable /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; start: 171/246) and make sure nothing that passed before regresses; also keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on your branch and report pass counts, features, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)

diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}

#!/bin/bash

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

import sys

from tw import tw
def m3(ws,g=32):
    xs=[0.0]
    for i in range(1,len(ws)):
        xs.append(xs[-1]+ws[i-1]/2+g+ws[i]/2)
    off=(xs[0]-ws[0]/2 + xs[-1]+ws[-1]/2)/2
    return [x-off for x in xs]
def m1(ws,g=32):
    tot=sum(ws)+g*(len(ws)-1)
    c=-tot/2; xs=[]
    for w in ws:
        xs.append(c+w/2); c+=w+g
    return xs
def m2(ws,g=32):
    tot=0.0
    for w in ws: tot+=w
    tot+=g*(len(ws)-1)
    c=0.0; xs=[]
    for w in ws:
        xs.append(c+w/2); c+=w+g
    return [x-tot/2 for x in xs]
def m4(ws,g=32):

    c=0.0; xs=[]
    for w in ws:
        xs.append(c+w/2); c+=w+g
    right=c-g
    off=right/2
    return [x-off for x in xs]

# Probe participant x positions via raw tab paths: each participant gets a
# loop with a self message, whose tab path starts at x - 23.5 (+4).
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile

def run(src, binp='/workspace/executable'):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/seq')
    open(os.path.join(d, 'p.lini'), 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'p.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])
    return r.stdout + r.stderr

def probe(labels, extra='', binp='/workspace/executable', gap=None):
    lines = ['{ layout: sequence%s }' % ('; gap: %s' % gap if gap else '')]
    for k, l in enumerate(labels):
        lines.append('|box#p%d| "%s"' % (k, l))
    lines.append(extra)
    for k in range(len(labels)):
        lines.append('|loop| [ p%d -> p%d ]' % (k, k))
    out = run('\n'.join(lines) + '\n', binp)
    xs = []
    for m in re.finditer(r'<path d="M (\S+) (\S+) L (\S+) \S+ L \S+ \S+ L \S+ \S+ L (\S+) ', out):
        xs.append(m.group(4))
    return xs, out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    labels = sys.argv[1:]
    xs, out = probe(labels)
    print(xs)

import sys

from tw import fonts
g = 32.0

def tws(s, size, w):
    t = fonts[w]
    advs = [t.adv[t.cmap[ord(c)]] for c in s]
    out = {}
    x = 0.0
    for a in advs: x += a / 1000 * size
    out['a/u*s'] = x
    x = 0.0
    for a in advs: x += a * size / 1000
    out['a*s/u'] = x
    out['sum*s/u'] = sum(advs) * size / 1000
    out['sum/u*s'] = sum(advs) / 1000 * size
    x = 0.0
    for a in advs: x += a * (size / 1000)
    out['a*(s/u)'] = x
    return out

def boxw(tw, k):
    if k == 0: return ((tw + 20) + 20) + 2
    if k == 1: return tw + 42
    if k == 2: return (tw + 2) + 40
    if k == 3: return tw + (20 + 20 + 2)

def curz(ws):
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for w in ws:
        xs.append(c + w/2); c += w + g
    tot = c - g
    return [x - tot/2 for x in xs]

def curz2(ws):
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for k, w in enumerate(ws):
        xs.append(c + w/2); c += w
        if k < len(ws) - 1: c += g
    tot = c
    return [x - tot/2 for x in xs]

def curz3(ws):
    # half-width steps
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for k, w in enumerate(ws):
        c += w / 2
        xs.append(c)
        c += w / 2 + g
    tot = c - g
    return [x - tot/2 for x in xs]

def curz4(ws):
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for k, w in enumerate(ws):
        if k: c += g
        xs.append(c + w/2); c += w
    return [x - c/2 for x in xs]

cases = {
    'CEabd': (['C', 'E', 'a', 'b', 'd'], ['-189.03500000000003', '-105.24750000000004', '-22.922500000000042', '59.76999999999998', '142.98000000000002']),
    'CSO': (['Customer', 'Storefront', 'Orders'], ['-158.71499999999997', '-13.29249999999999', '121.92249999999999']),
    'AB': (['A', 'B'], ['-65.15', '18.72']),
}
for var in ['a/u*s', 'a*s/u', 'sum*s/u', 'sum/u*s', 'a*(s/u)']:
    for k in range(4):
        for fn in [curz, curz2, curz3, curz4]:
            res = []
            for name, (labels, exp) in cases.items():
                ws = [boxw(tws(l, 15, 500)[var], k) for l in labels]
                xs = fn(ws)
                got = [repr(x - 23.5) for x in xs]
                res.append(got == exp)
            print(var, k, fn.__name__, res)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/scripts')
from tw import fonts
g = 32.0

def tws(s, size, w):
    t = fonts[w]
    advs = [t.adv[t.cmap[ord(c)]] for c in s]
    out = {}
    x = 0.0
    for a in advs: x += a / 1000 * size
    out['a/u*s'] = x
    x = 0.0
    for a in advs: x += a * size / 1000
    out['a*s/u'] = x
    out['sum*s/u'] = sum(advs) * size / 1000
    out['sum/u*s'] = sum(advs) / 1000 * size
    x = 0.0
    for a in advs: x += a * (size / 1000)
    out['a*(s/u)'] = x
    return out

def boxw(tw, k):
    if k == 0: return ((tw + 20) + 20) + 2
    if k == 1: return tw + 42
    if k == 2: return (tw + 2) + 40
    if k == 3: return tw + (20 + 20 + 2)

def curz(ws):
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for w in ws:
        xs.append(c + w/2); c += w + g
    tot = c - g
    return [x - tot/2 for x in xs]

def curz2(ws):
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for k, w in enumerate(ws):
        xs.append(c + w/2); c += w
        if k < len(ws) - 1: c += g
    tot = c
    return [x - tot/2 for x in xs]

def curz3(ws):
    # half-width steps
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for k, w in enumerate(ws):
        c += w / 2
        xs.append(c)
        c += w / 2 + g
    tot = c - g
    return [x - tot/2 for x in xs]

def curz4(ws):
    c = 0.0; xs = []
    for k, w in enumerate(ws):
        if k: c += g
        xs.append(c + w/2); c += w
    return [x - c/2 for x in xs]

cases = {
    'CEabd': (['C', 'E', 'a', 'b', 'd'], ['-189.03500000000003', '-105.24750000000004', '-22.922500000000042', '59.76999999999998', '142.98000000000002']),
    'CSO': (['Customer', 'Storefront', 'Orders'], ['-158.71499999999997', '-13.29249999999999', '121.92249999999999']),
    'AB': (['A', 'B'], ['-65.15', '18.72']),
}
for var in ['a/u*s', 'a*s/u', 'sum*s/u', 'sum/u*s', 'a*(s/u)']:
    for k in range(4):
        for fn in [curz, curz2, curz3, curz4]:
            res = []
            for name, (labels, exp) in cases.items():
                ws = [boxw(tws(l, 15, 500)[var], k) for l in labels]
                xs = fn(ws)
                got = [repr(x - 23.5) for x in xs]
                res.append(got == exp)
            print(var, k, fn.__name__, res)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Random sequence diagrams; compares the original with ours, prints failing seeds.
import random, subprocess, os, sys, tempfile

WORDS = ['login', 'fetch', 'save', 'ok', 'retry', 'token', 'POST /api', 'GET /items', 'validate', 'charge card',
         'reserve stock', 'notify', 'x', 'done', 'a much longer label for spacing', 'multi\\nline']
NAMES = ['user', 'web', 'api', 'db', 'cache', 'queue', 'svc', 'auth']
SHAPES = ['box', 'box', 'box', 'cyl', 'slant', 'oval', 'icon', 'hex', 'rect']
PAINT = ['', '', '', ' { fill: --sky-wash; stroke: --sky-deep; }', ' { fill: --rose-wash; }', ' { stroke: --orange-deep; stroke-width: 3; }']
OPS = ['->', '->', '->', '-->', '-->', '~>', '<-', '<->', '---']

def gen(rng):
    lines = []
    root = ['layout: sequence']
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        root.append('gap: %d %d' % (rng.choice([10, 20, 32, 48]), rng.choice([10, 24, 32, 60])))
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        root.append('activation: none')
    lines.append('{ %s; }' % '; '.join(root))
    k = rng.randint(1, 5)
    names = rng.sample(NAMES, k)
    declared = [n for n in names if rng.random() < 0.7]
    for n in declared:
        sh = rng.choice(SHAPES)
        if sh == 'icon':
            lines.append('|icon#%s| "%s"%s' % (n, rng.choice(['user', 'server', 'database']), rng.choice(PAINT)))
        else:
            lines.append('|%s#%s| "%s"%s' % (sh, n, n.capitalize(), rng.choice(PAINT)))
    def msg(ind):
        a = rng.choice(names); b = rng.choice(names) if rng.random() < 0.85 else a
        op = rng.choice(OPS)
        lab = ' "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ''
        return ind + '%s %s %s%s' % (a, op, b, lab)
    def note(ind):
        mode = rng.choice(['over', 'over', 'left', 'right'])
        if mode == 'over' and rng.random() < 0.5 and len(names) > 1:
            who = ' '.join(rng.sample(names, 2))
        else:
            who = rng.choice(names)
        return ind + '|note| "%s" { place: %s %s; }' % (rng.choice(WORDS), mode, who)
    def block(depth, ind):
        out = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4 if depth else 7)):
            r = rng.random()
            if r < 0.6:
                out.append(msg(ind))
            elif r < 0.72:
                out.append(note(ind))
            elif depth < 2:
                kind = rng.choice(['loop', 'alt', 'opt'])
                guard = ' "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ''
                pad = ' { padding: %d; }' % rng.choice([0, 10, 30]) if rng.random() < 0.2 else ''
                out.append(ind + '|%s|%s%s [' % (kind, guard, pad))
                out.extend(block(depth + 1, ind + '  '))
                if kind == 'alt' and rng.random() < 0.7:
                    out.append(ind + '  |else| "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS))
                    out.extend(block(depth + 1, ind + '  '))
                out.append(ind + ']')
        return out
    lines.extend(block(0, ''))
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

def run(binp, src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/seq')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'f.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'f.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])
    return r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr

start = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0
count = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100
bad = 0
os.makedirs('/tmp/seq/fz', exist_ok=True)
for seed in range(start, start + count):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    src = gen(rng)
    a = run('/workspace/executable', src)
    b = run('/tmp/bin-seq/executable', src)
    if a != b:
        bad += 1
        open('/tmp/seq/fz/s%d.lini' % seed, 'w').write(src)
        print('FAIL seed', seed, 'exit', a[0], b[0])
print('bad', bad, 'of', count)

    lines.append('{ %s; }' % '; '.join(root))
    k = rng.randint(1, 5)
    names = rng.sample(NAMES, k)
    declared = [n for n in names if rng.random() < 0.7]
    for n in declared:
        sh = rng.choice(SHAPES)
        if sh == 'icon':
            lines.append('|icon#%s| "%s"%s' % (n, rng.choice(['user', 'server', 'database']), rng.choice(PAINT)))
        else:
            lines.append('|%s#%s| "%s"%s' % (sh, n, n.capitalize(), rng.choice(PAINT)))
    def msg(ind):
        a = rng.choice(names); b = rng.choice(names) if rng.random() < 0.85 else a
        op = rng.choice(OPS)
        lab = ' "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ''
        return ind + '%s %s %s%s' % (a, op, b, lab)
    def note(ind):
        mode = rng.choice(['over', 'over', 'left', 'right'])
        if mode == 'over' and rng.random() < 0.5 and len(names) > 1:
            who = ' '.join(rng.sample(names, 2))
        else:
            who = rng.choice(names)
        return ind + '|note| "%s" { place: %s %s; }' % (rng.choice(WORDS), mode, who)
    def block(depth, ind):
        out = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4 if depth else 7)):
            r = rng.random()
            if r < 0.6:
                out.append(msg(ind))
            elif r < 0.72:
                out.append(note(ind))
            elif depth < 2:
                kind = rng.choice(['loop', 'alt', 'opt'])
                guard = ' "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ''
                pad = ' { padding: %d; }' % rng.choice([0, 10, 30]) if rng.random() < 0.2 else ''
                out.append(ind + '|%s|%s%s [' % (kind, guard, pad))
                out.extend(block(depth + 1, ind + '  '))
                if kind == 'alt' and rng.random() < 0.7:
                    out.append(ind + '  |else| "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS))
                    out.extend(block(depth + 1, ind + '  '))
                out.append(ind + ']')
        return out
    lines.extend(block(0, ''))
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

def run(binp, src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/seq')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'f.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'f.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])
    return r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr

import math, re
orig = open('/tmp/seq/o1.svg').read().split('\n')[128]
nums = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?', orig.split('d="')[1].split('"')[0])]
p0 = (107.915, 241.5)
p1 = (-96.6375, 241.5)
def f4(v):
    s = '%.4f' % v
    s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.') if '.' in s else s
    if s == '-0': s = '0'
    return s
def wave(p0, p1, var):
    l = math.hypot(p1[0] - p0[0], p1[1] - p0[1])
    u = ((p1[0] - p0[0]) / l, (p1[1] - p0[1]) / l)
    nrm = (-u[1], u[0])
    amp, lam, ramp = 1.4, 12.0, 6.0
    n = max(1, round(l / 3))
    h = l / n
    ss = lambda t: 3 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 2 - 2 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 3
    dss = lambda t: 0.0 if t <= 0 or t >= 1 else 6 * t - 6 * t * t
    w = 2 * math.pi / lam
    S = []
    for i in range(n + 1):
        x = i * h if var != 3 else l * i / n
        e1 = ss(x / ramp); e2 = ss((l - x) / ramp)
        if e1 < e2:
            e, de = e1, dss(x / ramp) / ramp
        else:
            e, de = e2, -dss((l - x) / ramp) / ramp
        y = amp * e * math.sin(w * x)
        dy = amp * (de * math.sin(w * x) + e * w * math.cos(w * x))
        S.append((x, y, dy))
    def to(x, y):
        if var in (0, 3):
            return (p0[0] + u[0] * x + nrm[0] * y, p0[1] + u[1] * x + nrm[1] * y)
        if var == 1:
            t = x / l
            return (p0[0] + (p1[0] - p0[0]) * t + nrm[0] * y, p0[1] + (p1[1] - p0[1]) * t + nrm[1] * y)
        if var == 2:
            return (p0[0] + (u[0] * x + nrm[0] * y), p0[1] + (u[1] * x + nrm[1] * y))
    out = [p0[0], p0[1]]
    for i in range(n):
        xa, ya, da = S[i]; xb, yb, db = S[i + 1]
        ch = math.hypot(xb - xa, yb - ya) / 3
        la = math.sqrt(1 + da * da); lb = math.sqrt(1 + db * db)
        c1 = to(xa + ch / la, ya + da / la * ch)
        c2 = to(xb - ch / lb, yb - db / lb * ch)
        e = to(xb, yb)
        out += [c1[0], c1[1], c2[0], c2[1], e[0], e[1]]
    return out
for var in range(4):
    got = wave(p0, p1, var)
    bad = sum(1 for a, b in zip(got, nums) if f4(a) != f4(b))
    print(var, len(got), len(nums), 'mismatches', bad)

exec(open('/tmp/seq/wv.py').read().split('def wave(')[0])
def wave2(p0, p1, xv, tv):
    l = math.hypot(p1[0] - p0[0], p1[1] - p0[1])
    u = ((p1[0] - p0[0]) / l, (p1[1] - p0[1]) / l)
    nrm = (-u[1], u[0])
    amp, lam, ramp = 1.4, 12.0, 6.0
    n = max(1, round(l / 3))
    h = l / n
    ss = lambda t: 3 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 2 - 2 * min(max(t, 0), 1) ** 3
    dss = lambda t: 0.0 if t <= 0 or t >= 1 else 6 * t - 6 * t * t
    w = 2 * math.pi / lam
    S = []
    for i in range(n + 1):
        if xv == 0: x = i * h
        elif xv == 1: x = l * i / n
        elif xv == 2: x = i * l / n
        elif xv == 3: x = (i / n) * l
        elif xv == 4: x = l * (i / n)
        e1 = ss(x / ramp); e2 = ss((l - x) / ramp)
        if e1 < e2:
            e, de = e1, dss(x / ramp) / ramp
        else:
            e, de = e2, -dss((l - x) / ramp) / ramp
        y = amp * e * math.sin(w * x)
        dy = amp * (de * math.sin(w * x) + e * w * math.cos(w * x))
        S.append((x, y, dy, i))
    def to(x, y, i=None):
        if tv == 0:
            return (p0[0] + u[0] * x + nrm[0] * y, p0[1] + u[1] * x + nrm[1] * y)
        if tv == 1:
            t = x / l
            return (p0[0] + (p1[0] - p0[0]) * t + nrm[0] * y, p0[1] + (p1[1] - p0[1]) * t + nrm[1] * y)
        if tv == 2:
            return (p0[0] * (1 - x / l) + p1[0] * (x / l) + nrm[0] * y, p0[1] * (1 - x / l) + p1[1] * (x / l) + nrm[1] * y)
    out = [p0[0], p0[1]]
    for i in range(n):

        e = to(xb, yb, ib)
        out += [c1[0], c1[1], c2[0], c2[1], e[0], e[1]]
    return out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Broader random sequence diagrams (styles, nesting, small gaps, labels).
import random, subprocess, os, sys, tempfile

WORDS = ['login', 'fetch', 'ok', 'token', 'POST /api', 'GET /items', 'charge card', 'x', 'done',
         'a much longer label for spacing', 'multi\\nline', 'three\\nline\\nlabel', 'é ü ✓', 'a & b']
NAMES = ['user', 'web', 'api', 'db', 'cache', 'queue', 'svc', 'auth', 'pay', 'shop']
SHAPES = ['box', 'box', 'box', 'cyl', 'slant', 'oval', 'icon', 'hex', 'rect', 'diamond']
PAINT = ['', '', '', ' { fill: --sky-wash; stroke: --sky-deep; }', ' { fill: --rose-wash; }',
         ' { stroke: --orange-deep; stroke-width: 3; }', ' { stroke: none; }', ' { padding: 10; }',
         ' { font-size: 18; }', ' { color: --green-deep; font-weight: bold; }']
OPS = ['->', '->', '->', '-->', '-->', '~>', '<-', '<->', '---', '*->', '-o<']
MSGSTYLE = ['', '', '', ' { stroke: --rose-deep; }', ' { stroke-width: 3; }', ' { stroke-style: dotted; }']
FRAMESTYLE = ['', '', '', ' { padding: 0; }', ' { padding: 10; }', ' { padding: 30; }', ' { fill: --purple-wash; stroke: --purple-ink; color: --gray-deep; }',
              ' { stroke-width: 2; }', ' { radius: 0; }', ' { font-size: 16; }']
NOTESTYLE = ['', '', ' fill: --rose-soft; stroke: --rose-deep;', ' font-size: 18;', ' padding: 2;', ' stroke-width: 1;']

def gen(rng):
    lines = []
    root = ['layout: sequence']
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        root.append('gap: %s %s' % (rng.choice([0, 6, 10, 20, 32, 48]), rng.choice([0, 10, 24, 32, 60])))
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        root.append('activation: none')
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        root.append('padding: %d' % rng.choice([0, 5, 40]))
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        root.append('font-size: %d' % rng.choice([12, 18]))
    nested = rng.random() < 0.2
    ind0 = ''
    if nested:
        lines.append('|box#outer| "Outer"')
        lines.append('|sequence|%s [' % rng.choice(['', ' { stroke: --stroke; }', ' { fill: --sky-wash; }', ' { gap: 16 20; }']))
        ind0 = '  '
    else:
        lines.append('{ %s; }' % '; '.join(root))
    k = rng.randint(1, 5)
    names = rng.sample(NAMES, k)
    declared = [n for n in names if rng.random() < 0.7]
    for n in declared:
        sh = rng.choice(SHAPES)
        if sh == 'icon':
            lines.append(ind0 + '|icon#%s| "%s"%s' % (n, rng.choice(['user', 'server', 'database']), rng.choice(['', ' { width: 48; }', ' { stroke: --rose-deep; fill: --rose-wash; }'])))
        else:
            lab = rng.choice([n.capitalize(), n.capitalize() + '\\nService', ''])
            lines.append(ind0 + '|%s#%s| "%s"%s' % (sh, n, lab, rng.choice(PAINT)))
    def msg(ind):
        a = rng.choice(names); b = rng.choice(names) if rng.random() < 0.85 else a
        op = rng.choice(OPS)
        lab = ' "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ''
        return ind + '%s %s %s%s%s' % (a, op, b, lab, rng.choice(MSGSTYLE))
    def note(ind):
        mode = rng.choice(['over', 'over', 'left', 'right'])
        if mode == 'over' and rng.random() < 0.5 and len(names) > 1:
            who = ' '.join(rng.sample(names, 2))
        else:
            who = rng.choice(names)
        return ind + '|note| "%s" { place: %s %s;%s }' % (rng.choice(WORDS), mode, who, rng.choice(NOTESTYLE))
    def block(depth, ind):
        out = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4 if depth else 7)):
            r = rng.random()
            if r < 0.6:
                out.append(msg(ind))
            elif r < 0.72:
                out.append(note(ind))
            elif depth < 2:
                kind = rng.choice(['loop', 'alt', 'opt'])
                guard = ' "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ''
                out.append(ind + '|%s|%s%s [' % (kind, guard, rng.choice(FRAMESTYLE)))
                out.extend(block(depth + 1, ind + '  '))
                if kind == 'alt' and rng.random() < 0.7:
                    out.append(ind + '  |else| "%s"' % rng.choice(WORDS))
                    out.extend(block(depth + 1, ind + '  '))
                out.append(ind + ']')
        return out
    lines.extend(block(0, ind0))
    if nested:
        lines.append(']')
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append('outer -> %s "into"' % rng.choice(['outer', 'z']))
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

def run(binp, src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/seq')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'f.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'f.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])
    return r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr

start = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0
count = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100
bad = 0
os.makedirs('/tmp/seq/fz2', exist_ok=True)
for seed in range(start, start + count):
    rng = random.Random(seed * 7919 + 13)
    src = gen(rng)
    a = run('/workspace/executable', src)
    b = run('/tmp/bin-seq/executable', src)
    if a != b:
        bad += 1
        open('/tmp/seq/fz2/s%d.lini' % seed, 'w').write(src)
        why = []
        if a[0] != b[0]: why.append('exit %d/%d' % (a[0], b[0]))
        if a[1] != b[1]: why.append('stdout')
        if a[2] != b[2]: why.append('stderr')
        print('FAIL seed', seed, ' '.join(why))
print('bad', bad, 'of', count)

import subprocess, re, os, tempfile, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/scripts')
from tw import fonts
def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/seq')
    open(os.path.join(d, 'p.lini'), 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'p.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])
    return r.stdout
t = fonts[500]
def adv(s): return [t.adv[t.cmap[ord(c)]] / 1000 * 13 for c in s]
def seq(v):
    s = 0.0
    for x in v: s += x
    return s
def tree(v):
    if len(v) == 1: return v[0]
    h = len(v) // 2
    return tree(v[:h]) + tree(v[h:])
texts = ['a very long message label here and more and more', 'starts checkout', 'rate-limited', 'the quick brown fox jumps over', 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz', 'Hello World Again and Again']
for txt in texts:
    out = run('{ layout: sequence }\n|box#a|\n|note| "%s" { place: over a; padding: 0; stroke: none }\n' % txt)
    m = re.search(r'<path d="M (\S+) ', out)
    hw = -float(m.group(1))
    v = adv(txt)
    print(repr(txt), repr(hw), 'seq', repr(seq(v) / 2), 'tree', repr(tree(v) / 2))

import subprocess, re, os, tempfile
def run(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/seq')
    open(os.path.join(d, 'p.lini'), 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'p.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    subprocess.run(['rm', '-rf', d])
    return r.stdout
for n in range(1, 16):
    txt = 'x' * n
    out = run('{ layout: sequence; font-family: mono }\n|box#a|\n|note| "%s" { place: over a; padding: 0; stroke: none }\n' % txt)
    m = re.search(r'<path d="M (\S+) ', out)
    hw = float(m.group(1)) * -1 if m else None

    s = 0.0
    for _ in range(n): s += 600 / 1000 * 13

    b = n * 0.6 * 13
    c = n * 600 * 13 / 1000
    dd = 600 * n / 1000 * 13
    print(n, repr(hw), [repr(v / 2) for v in (a, b, c, dd)])

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

`layout: sequence` is finished and committed on `worktree-agent-ad160a1e655787e4c` (commits a2a3f12 to ac525a2, working tree clean). All 10 sequence test files now match the original byte for byte, with no regressions.

**Pass counts** (rebuilt and re-run just now with `/tmp/bin-seq/executable`):
- Full asset comparison: **182 / 246**, up from 171.
- The 11 newly passing files are prop_activation, prop_place, skill_04, spec_31, spec_32 (the error case), spec_55, test_samples/sequence, blocks/skill_004, blocks/spec_031 and blocks/spec_055. The eleventh is test_samples/cards, fixed by a root font-family change.
- `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"` and `-a highlight` are all still **246 / 246**.
- Checked earlier, also with no regressions: `--json` went from 208 to 209 and `--theme dark` from 165 to 176.
- My own corpus of about 350 small sequence cases matches except 3, all caused by the general problems listed under gaps. Random sequence inputs from three generators (150+ cases each in the latest runs) found no mismatches.

**What it covers** (nearly all in the new `src/sequence.rs`, about 1,700 lines):
- **Participants:** any node type, painted onto their lifelines and bars, created automatically when a message names them, at the root or as a nested `|sequence|`. The default gap is 32 32, and the horizontal positions reproduce the original's float rounding exactly.
- **Messages:** kept in source order. `->` opens an activation bar, `-->` returns and `~>` is async. Self-messages (including wavy loops) don't open or close bars, and `activation: none` turns bars off. Labels reuse the existing link label and mask helpers, and paths print raw f64 where the original does.
- **Frames:** `|loop|`, `|opt|` and `|alt|` with `|else|`, including tabs, guards (multi-line too) and else dividers.
- **Notes:** `place: over a b`, `left a` or `right a`, with their own default padding and font size.
- **Errors and warnings:** the misplaced-frame and misplaced-`|else|` errors, a note without `place`, a malformed `place`, a sequence with no participants, and the `activation`/`place` property checks (now mapped to codes V002, V007 and V008). Also the "auto-creates a new box; did you mean …?" typo warning.

**Edits to shared files:**
- `main.rs`: the module, a pre-check pass and a validation pass.
- `layout.rs`: one dispatch line to the sequence measurer.
- `links.rs`: links get a `seq` flag so messages get sequence geometry and labels, plus a `.lini-sequence-message` style rule and wavy message paths. Three general fixes affect all links:
  - mask size is now span plus margins;
  - wave sample points are now spaced `l*i/n` along the line;
  - link labels now carry the font-family.
- `render.rs`: hooks for root and nested sequences, new style slots, and a shared `bbox_walk`. General changes outside sequences:
  - the root font-family replaces the themed font stack (this is the cards fix);
  - a class's dash now matches its own stroke width, and nodes wearing it carry their actual dash inline where it differs;
  - zero-size non-block shapes still draw;
